_meta.purpose: Pre-resolved registry values for downstream agents. Agents consuming this file do NOT need to load raw registry files.

spec_identity.notes: New spec. TSK_WDWL_* not in context_prefixes_in_use — no collision. Combined prime+paint spec (primer conditional on substrate_state). Domain: interior, context: NC. SF-based wood wall panel/board measurement. wall_style (flat_panel/shiplap/tongue_and_groove/library_panel) is a configuration dimension driving complexity modifier. Height varies (PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND applies) — key distinction from SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC (always H1).

paintable_items.name: Wood wall panel/board surface
paintable_items.notes: Single SF item for entire wood wall surface (panels or boards + internal rails/stiles for library_panel + applied molding). Measured as total wall area covered by wood surface from floor to ceiling. Internal complexity captured by wall_style modifier. No cap rail — wood wall meets ceiling directly.

task_prefix.collision_check: No collision. TSK_WDWL_* not in context_prefixes_in_use. Checked against all existing prefixes: FLOOR_PROTECT, DUST_WIPE, LIGHT_SAND, EDGE_SEAL, SPOT_FILL, CAULK, PRIME_*, FINISH_*, INTERSTAGE_SAND, FINAL_INSPECT, FRAME_*, DOOR_*, CEIL_*, WALL_*, TRIM_*, WIN_*, STRS_*, WNSC_*.
task_prefix.naming_rule: TSK_WDWL_{ACTION} — action should be verb-based (FLOOR_PROTECT, CEILING_MASK, DUST_CLEAN, SAND_PREP, FILL_FASTENERS, CAULK_JOINTS, CAULK_PERIMETER, SEAL_MDF_EDGES, PRIME_FACES, FINISH_SPRAY, FINISH_BRUSH, SAND_BETWEEN, INSPECT_COAT, FINAL_INSPECT, REMOVE_PROTECTION, REMOVE_CEILING_MASK, VACUUM)

expected_modules.description: Floor protection, ceiling masking (spray only), staging.
Dust wipe, sand per substrate/QT, fill fastener holes, caulk board/panel joints, caulk perimeter (wall-to-ceiling and wall-to-floor junctions), MDF edge seal (bare MDF only).
Primer coat — conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE. Primer type driven by substrate (MDF two-step, FJP stain-block, softwood standard, hardwood tannin-block).
Finish coat application. Spray: sweep passes following board direction (shiplap/T&G) or broad passes (flat_panel) or field-then-frame (library_panel). Brush: panel-to-frame sequence.
Between-coat inspect, sand, repair — universal at ALL quality tiers. Rigid block sanding per FFD §15.4.1. Flexible sanding sponge for grooves/profiles.
Final quality check. Visual inspection at tier-appropriate distance. Check holidays in grooves (shiplap/T&G) and at panel-to-frame transitions (library_panel).
Protection teardown, ceiling mask removal, floor vacuum, tool cleaning.

module_prefix.notes: Combined prime+paint spec. Prime module conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE. No internal component sequencing needed — single SF item. Height varies per room — estimation engine applies height modifier via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND.

paintscope_keys.description: Total SF of wood paneled wall surface from floor to ceiling. Includes board faces and joint detail (shiplap, T&G) or panels, internal rails/stiles, and applied molding (flat_panel, library_panel).
paintscope_keys.notes: Primary input for this spec. No existing key covers full-height wood wall surfaces. PS_SURFACE_SF.WALL_FIELD is for drywall. PS_SURFACE_SF.WAINSCOTING is for partial-height wainscot. Semantically distinct surface.

paintscope_keys.description: Floor protection area at wood wall work zone.
Ceiling masking LF at ceiling-wall junction. Spray only.
paintscope_keys.notes: Conditional on application_method = spray. Zone exists in Protection_Zones_Reference.md but PS key and zone_id not yet in id_registry active entries. Needs activation.

paintscope_keys.description: Height classification for modifier selection — wood wall height varies by room. Values: STD (0-8 ft), STEP (9-12 ft), EXT (13-17 ft), SCAFFOLD (18-24 ft), LIFT (25+ ft).
paintscope_keys.notes: Exists in PaintScope Quantity Key Catalog (Modifier Meta Keys section) but not in id_registry PS_ entries_in_active_use. Needs activation. KEY distinction from SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC (always H1). Estimation engine applies height modifier per room.

quality_tier.notes: QT2 not applicable — wood walls are prominent millwork per Millwork Doctrine §6.

application_method.notes: Spray preferred for NC production — large flat wall areas spray efficiently. Brush for occupied spaces, small areas, or touch-up. No backroll method — wood panel surfaces do not require backrolling.

wall_style.notes: Spec-specific configuration dimension. Drives production rate complexity modifier: flat_panel=1.0x, shiplap=1.15x, tongue_and_groove=1.10x, library_panel=1.25x. Per Millwork Doctrine §7.2 complexity categories.

sheen.notes: Sheen/QT gate: satin at QT3+, semi-gloss at QT4+, gloss at QT5 only. Satin default for softer appearance on large wood wall surfaces.

substrate_state.notes: SS_BARE requires primer (substrate-driven chemistry). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips primer. Standard NC delivery is factory-primed.

unit_of_measure.notes: SF for wood wall panel tasks. EA_ROOM for room-level setup/cleanup. LF for ceiling masking protection. FIXED for tool cleanup.

product_role.notes: Combined prime+paint spec. Sealer for MDF edge sealing (solvent-based).

protection_level.notes: edge_only for floor_perimeter. light_mask for ceiling_line (spray only).

surface_texture.notes: Wood wall panel/board surfaces are smooth.

modifier_mechanism.notes: QT3=baseline, QT4/QT5=selective_multiplier on qt_scaled tasks, QT5 brush=additional_rounds.

surface_ids.notes: wall_panel exists in Surface_Vocabulary_Reference.md Wall Surfaces section but not yet in id_registry active entries — needs activation. All adjacent surface IDs are existing. Key distinction from wainscot: wainscot uses trim_wainscot_rail (cap rail); wood wall uses ceiling_field (direct ceiling junction) and trim_crown (when crown molding present).

zone_ids.notes: Drop cloth runners at base of wood wall work area. Always required regardless of application method.

Paper masking at ceiling-wall junction — spray only. Zone exists in Protection_Zones_Reference.md (Surface-Adjacent Protection Zones table) but not in id_registry zone_ids entries_in_active_use. Needs activation. Key distinction from wainscot: wainscot uses wall_adjacent (masking wall above cap rail); wood wall uses ceiling_line (masking ceiling at wall-ceiling junction).

primer_systems.name: Solvent-based MDF edge sealer
primer_systems.notes: Reuse from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC. Step 1 of two-step MDF prime. Water-based causes irreversible fiber swelling.

primer_systems.name: High-build latex face primer for MDF
primer_systems.notes: Reuse from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC. Step 2 of two-step MDF prime.

primer_systems.name: Stain-blocking primer for FJP/poplar
primer_systems.notes: Reuse from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC. MANDATORY for bare FJP — blocks green mineral streak bleed-through.

primer_systems.name: Tannin-blocking primer for hardwood
primer_systems.notes: Reuse from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC. Blocks tannin bleed-through on bare hardwood (oak, cherry, walnut).

primer_systems.name: Acrylic wood primer for softwood
primer_systems.notes: Reuse from SF_WINDOW_INT_NC. Standard acrylic primer-sealer for bare softwood.

material_system_prefix.notes: All material systems reuse existing IDs. 3 finish systems (SYS_FF_*) + 5 primer systems (SYS_PRIMER_*). No new system IDs needed. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005). Identical primer chemistry matrix to SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC.

consumable_prefix.notes: All consumables reuse existing CON_ IDs. No new consumable IDs needed. Board-style walls (shiplap, T&G) consume significantly more CON_SPACKLE_LIGHTWEIGHT due to high fastener hole density — Materials Manager should note elevated consumption.

proposed_for_this_spec.description: Wood wall panel primer coverage rate
Wood wall panel finish coat coverage rate

cross_spec_coordination.notes: No cross-spec flags. Wood wall work pairs with SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT for adjacent trim in same finish group (baseboard, crown, casings) and SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH for adjacent drywall wall at transitions. No cap rail — crown molding (when present) handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT.

cross_file_threading: RULE 1: Every TSK_ in sop_modules.json MUST have a matching rate in production.json
RULE 2: Every ITM_ in spec.json MUST appear in at least one variant
RULE 3: Every SYS_ quality_tier MUST match spec.json configuration_dimensions
RULE 4: Every IN_ input in spec.json SHOULD be consumed by sop_modules or production
RULE 5: Every PS_ key in production.json MUST match spec.json required_paintscope_inputs
RULE 6: Every zone_id in spec.json MUST match sop_modules.json protection_metadata.zones
RULE 7: Module phase order: setup > prep > prime > apply > interstage > finish > cleanup
RULE 8: UOM for a task MUST match between sop_modules.json and production.json
RULE 9: TSK_ prefix from resolution.json MUST be used in sop_modules and production
RULE 10: ITM_ IDs marked existing in resolution.json MUST use exact registered ID in spec.json
RULE 11: Downstream agents MUST use only enum values in resolution.json applicable_enums
